'''''Phlomoides tuberosa''''' ([[synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] '''''Phlomis tuberosa'''''), the '''sage-leaf mullein''',<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/504476/phlomoides-tuberosa/details | title = ''Phlomoides tuberosa'' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 6 June 2022}}</ref> is a [[perennial plant|perennial]] [[herbaceous]] flowering plant in the family [[Lamiaceae]], native to China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Russia, south west Asia and Europe. Enlarged, tuberous roots give rise to erect stems to 150 cm bearing purple-red flowers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Flora of China|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200020019|website=eFloras|publisher=Flora of China Project|access-date=8 December 2016|ref=FOC}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
This plant is grown in full sun, but may tolerate some shade.<ref name = RHSPF/> The [[cultivar]] 'Amazone' has won the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/72387/Phlomis-tuberosa-Amazone/Details | title = ''Phlomis tuberosa'' 'Amazone' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref>

==Uses==
The [[Kalmyks]] are said to have eaten the cooked root, calling the plant ''bodmon sok''.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Pickering|first1=Charles|title=Chronological History of Plants|date=1879|publisher=Little, Brown, and Company|location=Boston|page=793|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/115487#page/821/mode/1up|access-date=8 December 2016|ref=CHoP}}</ref> Another source for [[Mongolia]] has the plant used as a folk restorative medicine against intoxication, tuberculosis, pulmonary and cardiovascular diseases and rheumatoid arthritis.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal|last1=Yang|first1=Yingbo|last2=Gu|first2=Lihua|last3=Xiao|first3=Ying|last4=Liu|first4=Qing|last5=Hu|first5=Haijun|last6=Wang|first6=Zhengtao|last7=Chen|first7=Kaixian|title=Rapid Identification of α-Glucosidase Inhibitors from Phlomis tuberosa by Sepbox Chromatography and Thin-Layer Chromatography Bioautography|journal=PLOS ONE|date=2015|volume=10|issue=2|article-number=e0116922|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0116922|pmid=25658100|ref=Rapid PLoS|pmc=4319760|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Buryats|Buryat]] [[lama]]s used some part of the plant to treat diarrhoea, eye and lung disease and as a sedative.<ref name="Phlom-Essent"/>
